translation: Target is defined as a proposition (it is not asserted or proved) that makes no reference to any of the preceding context definitions (S1, S2, S3, etc.). It states: for all types X1 (in universe u), X2 (in universe v), and E (in universe w), and for all functions g : X1 → X2 and c2 : X1 → E, there exist a type X (in the same universe w as E), a function h : X1 → X, and a function c4 : X2 × X → E (all of which may depend on X1, X2, E, g, and c2), such that for every s in X1, c2 s = c4 (g s, h s). There are no additional hypotheses on X1, X2, E, g, or c2 (such as finiteness or nonemptiness), and no additional constraints on X, h, or c4 beyond their types and the equation c2 s = c4 (g s, h s)—in particular, X is not constrained in size or structure (and lives in the same universe as E), h is not constrained to be distinct from or independent of c2 or g, and c4 is not required to depend on its first argument in X2.

divergences.description: All three passages concern specifically first-person conscious experiences, and [P-K52] distinguishes datasets determined by physical configurations P alone from those determined by conscious experience in E. In Target, the extra observable is an unconstrained extensional function h : X1 → X on the same domain X1 as g and c2, so the formalization cannot distinguish first-person evidence from third-person internal observables of the system, nor express [P-K52]'s causal/ontological distinction between dependence on P versus dependence on E (minor given the author's explicit scoping to the bare logical content of adding some further observable).

Target is completely detached from the S1 and S3 definitions in the context: it generalizes i/o behaviour to an arbitrary function g : X1 → X2 (a harmless strengthening) and idealizes the Kleiner-Hoel dataset layer in [P-K52]/S3 (where physical configurations yield sets of datasets D with inference content R and set-valued predictions Set E) into total, single-valued functions g : X1 → X2 and c2 : X1 → E directly on X1, implicitly ruling out empty prediction sets for which no extra observable could avoid mismatch.

Because the existential quantifier over the observable (X, h) sits inside the universal quantifier over theories c2, Target allows the observable h to depend on the theory being evaluated (e.g., h = c2), establishing only that no theory is forced to mismatch rather than modelling a single theory-independent 'ground truth' first-person observable as in [P-H9] that confirms true theories while falsifying false ones (minor since this matches the author's explicit claim about the extreme case where the observable is the predicted experience itself).

judgement.summary: Target accurately captures the narrow, intentionally trivial logical point claimed by the author—that allowing an inference map to use an arbitrary additional function of the system removes any forced mismatch with a theory's predictions. Its divergences from the source passages are minor idealizations and expressive limitations inherent in the bare extensional formulation (omitting the dataset/set-valued structure of S3, the theory-independent 'ground truth' role of first-person experience, and the distinction between observables determined by P versus E).
